findings.text: Global idle entry hook for tickless balancing. When the calling processor goes idle it records that blocked load may exist, records that its tick is stopped unless already recorded, joins the set of idle processors, publishes scheduler domain idle state and requests global blocked load and next balance updates. Processors going offline do nothing and fully isolated processors do not join tickless balancing.

Global per processor handler for deferred tickless work. It atomically clears the new idle balance kick indicator and only when that was the sole pending reason and no reschedule is pending it refreshes blocked statistics for stopped tick idle processors. An alternate header form provides an empty definition when the feature is disabled.

Global setter that associates the current run queue with its present low power idle state. One header variant stores the state pointer into the run queue while the alternate variant discards the request when idle state tracking is disabled.

Global reference counted control for forcing polling idle instead of deep sleep. Enabling increments the counter and disabling decrements it with a one time warning on underflow. Separate early boot options force the counter to enabled or disabled.

Weak architecture hooks for idle preparation, entry, exit, terminal offline sleep and default sleep, overridable by each architecture. The generic defaults do nothing except that terminal sleep never returns and generic sleep forces future polling. A generic idle routine wraps the architecture sleep with polling, broadcast, tracing and timing handling.

Soft interrupt handler for periodic load balancing. It first attempts tickless balancing on behalf of idle processors with stopped ticks and returns if such work was pending. Otherwise it refreshes blocked averages for the local processor and then balances scheduling domains.

Main idle execution path. After handling offline termination and deferred tickless updates, it enters a loop that disables interrupts, notifies architecture entry, flushes deferred wakeups, then either polls with interrupts enabled or delegates to the cpuidle selector. On wakeup it propagates the reschedule request, exits tickless idle handling, clears polling, orders memory, flushes inter processor work and invokes the idle scheduler.

Blocked statistics for a run queue are refreshed only when that queue advertises blocked load, remains a member of the idle set, and its minimum refresh interval has elapsed. Queues without the advertisement report no work, queues that left the idle set report no work, and queues refreshed recently report that work remains without refreshing again.

Tickless balancing clears the global blocked load and needs update indicators only when the corresponding kick reasons are present, then orders memory before scanning the idle set so that a concurrent idle entry cannot be missed. The scan starts after the local processor to favor work sharing and tracks the earliest future balance time across visited queues.

During the tickless scan each still idle processor has its blocked statistics optionally refreshed and, when its individual balance deadline has arrived, its clock updated under lock with domain balancing attempted for idle type when requested. At completion the global next balance is published only if at least one visited queue contributed, and the next blocked refresh deadline is set to the current time plus the load averaging period.

Per run queue tickless work is represented by a flag word that is tested and cleared on entry. If no work is pending nothing happens, if the processor is not in the deepest idle type no work happens despite pending flags, and an alternate build provides a form that always reports no work.

Bringing a fair run queue online refreshes control parameters and runtime enablement. Taking it offline refreshes control parameters, makes throttled groups reachable for task selection, and removes the departing queue contribution from group shares.

The fair class periodic tick walks the current entity hierarchy when queued, updating each level and propagating proportional weight, then reweights the leaf for earliest virtual deadline scheduling. If the tick arrived in queued context it stops there, otherwise it additionally updates NUMA behavior, cache behavior, misfit status, overutilization status and core scheduling behavior.

Slice exhaustion is judged by comparing consumed runtime scaled by a task count against the entity slice. Under core scheduling, when force idle pressure exists on the core and the local fair queue holds exactly one runnable entity that has exhausted its slice under an assumed sibling load, the current task is asked to reschedule. An alternate build provides an empty core tick.

Priority changes for non queued tasks, unchanged priority values, and single task queues cause no action. For a running task whose priority numerically increased the processor is asked to reschedule, while for a non running queued task a wakeup preemption check is performed.

Throttle state for a task on a processor is determined by the throttle state of its group hierarchy on that processor, using per group queues when grouping is enabled and the local fair queue otherwise. Forking only records maximum allowed capacity, and the round robin interval is zero on an otherwise idle queue and otherwise derived from the task slice converted to timer ticks.

Leaving the fair class detaches the entity from its fair queue, with delayed entities first removed from the run queue under sleep plus delayed semantics. Joining the fair class attaches the entity, records capacity, warns if still delayed, and either requests rescheduling when running or checks preemption when queued. Selecting the next fair task clears buddy hints, removes the entity if queued, walks the hierarchy installing next entities and accounting runtime with throttling setup if needed, then publishes the leaf, reweights, protects the slice on first selection, moves the group node to most recently used order and updates hrtick, misfit and tick stop state.

Group changes for tasks that have never been woken are ignored. Otherwise the task is detached from its old fair queue, its averaging timestamp is cleared to force a fresh start, its processor assignment is refreshed and it is attached to the new group queue.

Cpuidle entry returns immediately with interrupts enabled when rescheduling is pending. When drivers are unavailable it adjusts tick handling then uses the generic idle path. Suspend to idle or forced latency limits select the deepest allowed state with tick stopped, multi state drivers consult the governor which may revise tick stopping and later reflect on the outcome, and single state drivers always use state zero.

Polling idle enables interrupts and spins while rescheduling is not requested and either forced polling is active or broadcast expiry is indicated, with tracing and timing notifications around the spin. Tick stopping in idle is chosen when requested or already stopped, otherwise the tick is retained, and broadcast enter and exit are either gated by a static key or compiled to no operations.

A dedicated mutex serializes fair group share updates. The tickless scan acquires each visited run queue lock with interrupts saved only to advance its clock, releasing before any domain balancing. Marking blocked load on idle entry needs no run queue lock, while the corresponding check and clear are performed with ordering that pairs with the idle entry barrier.

Run queue state observed here includes processor identity, blocked load flag, tick stopped flag, last blocked update time, next balance time, per queue tickless work flags, idle balance type, idle state pointer, fair queue and fair task list, and core scheduling control with force idle count. Global tickless state includes an idle processor mask, blocked load and needs update indicators, and next balance and next blocked deadlines.

Scheduling entities expose total and previous runtime, slice, queue membership, delayed state, group linkage and averaging timestamp. Fair queues expose load weight, queued count, current and hierarchy current pointers. Cpuidle devices expose last residency and forced latency limit, while drivers expose state count.

Tickless kick reasons form a lifecycle where idle entry sets global blocked and update requests, per queue work accumulates, the soft interrupt consumes per queue work, the scanner clears globals then re arms them if work remains or if the local processor gained work mid scan, and a separate new balance kick is cleared by the idle loop with stats only handling when isolated.

Fair class membership moves through attach, running selection and detach. Delayed tasks are dequeued before leaving, detachment drops group linkage, attachment restores it with capacity recording, and first time selection arms high resolution tick and tick stop updates while later selections skip those one time actions.

Processor idle moves from tickless update and polling setup into a sleeping loop and then to reschedule propagation and scheduling. Inside the loop each iteration disables interrupts, enters architecture idle, chooses polling when forced or broadcast expired and cpuidle otherwise, records whether the tick fired, exits architecture idle, and repeats until rescheduling is requested.

Entering tickless idle on a processor other than the caller, decrementing the poll counter below zero, attaching a still delayed entity, selecting a delayed next task, taking an offline processor with pending reschedule, and leaving cpuidle with interrupts disabled are all treated as one time warnings with defined recovery such as enabling interrupts.

If the local processor gains work mid scan and needs rescheduling, the tickless scan aborts and re arms the corresponding global indicators so the next owner resumes the work. Cpuidle helpers recheck polling after clearing it and abort entry with a busy status when a wakeup arrived, avoiding lost wakeups and stale residency accounting.

Idle entry orders the idle mask publication before the global indicators so a scanner that misses the mask must observe the indicators, and the scanner orders its flag clearing before the mask scan. Idle exit orders polling clearance before pending wakeup processing and requires interrupts to remain disabled until the sleep instruction or equivalent rollback protection to avoid missing timer reprogramming.
The assumed minimum runnable count used to judge slice exhaustion during forced idle is two.
Nanosecond to timer tick conversion divides by the number of nanoseconds per second divided by the tick rate.
The tickless scan initializes its next balance candidate to the current time plus sixty seconds.
